context: Current closing price of Electronic Arts (EA): $209.70 USD as of 2026-11-11.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift assumption from what appears to be a baseline price around $209–$210. At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing price, adding only a slight positive drift to arrive at $210.5, since overnight and next-session moves for most liquid assets tend to be small relative to longer-horizon uncertainty. At the one-week horizon, I projected $211.8, incorporating a continued but gentle upward trend while acknowledging that a week provides enough time for meaningful price discovery and repositioning. At the one-month horizon, $214.0 reflects a compounding of that drift assumption, though I held it relatively modest because mean-reversion tendencies and shifting macro conditions can easily offset short-term momentum over four-plus weeks.

The confidence interval widths were primarily driven by the typical scaling of volatility with the square root of time. At one day, the interval is quite tight ($204–$217, a range of $13) because short-horizon realized volatility for most equity-like instruments is relatively constrained in the absence of a known catalyst. At one week, the interval widens to $199–$224 ($25 range) to account for the accumulation of daily price shocks and the possibility of a mid-week macro surprise. At one month, the interval expands substantially to $188–$240 ($52 range), reflecting that over four weeks, earnings releases, Federal Reserve communications, geopolitical developments, and sector-specific news could all compound to drive substantial moves in either direction.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include an unexpected large macro shock — such as a surprise central bank policy shift, a geopolitical escalation, or a sudden credit event — which could easily produce moves beyond the outer bounds of even my one-month interval. On the upside, a strongly positive earnings surprise or a risk-on rally driven by better-than-expected economic data could push prices well above $240. On the downside, a broad equity selloff, liquidity crisis, or sector-specific regulatory action could breach the $188 lower bound. My intervals are calibrated for typical market conditions, and tail events by definition fall outside the 90% confidence band I've specified, meaning there remains a 10% probability — split across both tails — that the true outcome lands outside these ranges even under normal circumstances.
